# A ball with a one-limb center from an interval of two limbs

Kernel `ball_from_interval_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains the interval $[l_o, h_i]$ of two values of `T`, with the exact midpoint for its center when halving is exact; or the whole line, or the empty set:

$$Z \supseteq [l_o, h_i].$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $h_i$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball.
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other: $Z$ is the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$).
- If $l_o \le h_i$, both finite: $Z$ is a finite ball that contains $[l_o, h_i]$.
- Then $l_o \le c_w \le h_i$ and $\lvert c_w - \tfrac{l_o + h_i}{2}\rvert \le u\,\lvert \tfrac{l_o + h_i}{2}\rvert + \eta$, and $r_w = \mathrm{RU}(\max(c_w - l_o, h_i - c_w))$, the smallest radius of `T` for that center.
- If $l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$, $h_i > -\infty$ and a bound is infinite: $Z$ is the whole line.
- Otherwise ($l_o > h_i$, $[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the empty set.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_from_interval_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_from_interval_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`interval_make_1`](interval_make_1.md), [`interval_to_ball_1`](interval_to_ball_1.md).

```
# A ball with a one-limb center from an interval [lo, hi] of two values of T supplied by the program
# (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", "A ball from an interval of two T"): interval_make_1,
# which guards the bounds (rule R3), followed by interval_to_ball_1, as the page says of Ball<T, 1>
# from two T. So it has the three cases of ball_from_interval_2: a NaN bound gives the whole line
# through the whole-line interval, lo > hi, [+inf, +inf] and [-inf, -inf] the empty ball through the
# empty interval, and an interval with an infinite bound the whole line; finite bounds lo <= hi give
# the ball of interval_to_ball_1: its center within u |m| + eta of the midpoint m and in [lo, hi], and
# the smallest radius of T for that center.

(zl, zu) = interval_make_1(lo, hi)
(cw, rw) = interval_to_ball_1(zl, zu)
```
